title: Carbapenems plus clavulanate
dek: Meropenem or imipenem with clavulanate (to block BlaC) is Group C salvage. It is IV, expensive, and not BPaLM. BlaC explains why a carbapenem alone looked silly in 2009 broths.
story: M. tuberculosis expresses BlaC, an Ambler class A β-lactamase that eats many β-lactams. Clavulanate inhibits BlaC enough that meropenem (or imipenem) can inhibit peptidoglycan synthesis in some isolates. WHO lists carbapenem+clavulanate in Group C for longer individualised DR-TB when A/B drugs are insufficient.

This is not oral, not cheap, and not a substitute for BDQ/LZD. Dosing is multiple-times-daily IV. Amoxicillin–clavulanate supplies the clavulanate in many protocols; the amoxicillin is not the active anti-TB idea.

No tidy RRDR-like carbapenem resistance hotspot in routine catalogues. Do not invent a blaC SNP as a WHO-grade call without a catalogue row. Prior β-lactam exposure in NTM clinics is a different species.
deep: Without clavulanate, carbapenem MICs look terrible; with it, some isolates look interesting. Always read the companion.
Ertapenem is not the TB carbapenem of record.
Pregnancy salvage sometimes lands here when injectables are forbidden and Pa is off — still a specialist construct.
Do not combine with other unexplained experimental β-lactams from Twitter.

visual.caption: BlaC eats carbapenems until clavulanate blocks it. Then meropenem can reach peptidoglycan transpeptidases. Group C, not Group A.
